memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Abram said, "Sovereign Lord, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?" And Abram said, "You have given me no children; so a servant in my household will be my heir." - Gen 15:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God has just made a magnificent promise, and Abram's response is startlingly blunt: "What can you give me since I remain childless?" He essentially says, Lord, what good is any of this? You've given me no children. There is pain here, and frustration, and something close to complaint.

And notice - God does not rebuke him. He doesn't say, "How dare you question Me." He listens, and then He answers. God can handle our honesty.

Many of us think prayer must be polite and polished, that we must hide our disappointment behind pious language. But Scripture is full of raw, honest prayer. The Psalms cry, "How long, Lord? Will you forget me forever?" (Ps 13:1). God is not fragile. He would rather have our honest ache than our dishonest composure.

Notice too that Abram brings his complaint to God, not about Him to others. That is the crucial difference between honest prayer and mere grumbling. He takes his pain to the only One who can do anything about it. "Pour out your hearts to him, for God is our refuge" (Ps 62:8). Whatever ache you have been dressing up in polite words - bring it honestly to the God who can bear it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you honest with God, or do you dress up your prayers?
- What disappointment do you need to bring directly to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You can handle my honesty. Forgive me for hiding my real feelings behind polite words. I bring You my actual ache today, trusting You are strong enough to receive it.
Amen.
